steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Lightly grease a cookie sheet.

Beat eggs in a large bowl. Stir in milk, water, salt, and bacon fat until well blended. Gradually stir in flour to make a stiff dough. Pinch off pieces of the dough and roll into 2 inch balls. Place on prepared baking sheet.
Bake in preheated oven for 35 to 40 minutes. Cool on racks. Store in a covered container in the refrigerator.

raw_recipe.headline: Bacon-Flavored Dog Biscuits
raw_recipe.description: Easy-to-make, bacon-flavored doggie treats are rolled from a whole wheat dough, then baked into crisp cookies.
raw_recipe.name: Bacon-Flavored Dog Biscuits

review.reviewBody: I added an extra egg, powdered milk, chicken broth in place of the water, half a jar of peanut butter, and crumbled bacon. I also used 1 cup of rolled oats in place of 3/4 cup of the whole wheat flour. The beauty of this recipe is that you can add in just about anything that can be mixed easily, and it will work. Used part rendered beef fat since I only had 3 strips of bacon. I wasn't up to rolling and cutting, so I just rolled little balls and flattened them to bake. You can pack them closely together on the baking sheet, since they don't expand as they bake. Remember to store in the fridge, as they don't contain preservatives and will get moldy in time. I feel good about giving these out as treats because they're all natural and I know exactly what went into them. My Westie, my daughter's mixed breed and her boyfriend's puggle will do back flips to get their jaws around one of these! Edited to add:No need to buy bacon. Save all trimmings from steak, chicken (plus skin,) pork,etc. in the freezer. When you have a handful or two, render (fry on low for about 15-20 minutes to melt off the fat.) Chop up the pieces left in the rendering pan and put them in the mix with the rendered fat. No expensive bacon needed. That's stuff you'd normally throw in the trash. You're recycling, AND your doggie will go nuts - promise!

I made this with a few modifications and it got a big paws-up from my dogs. I cut all the ingredients in half except the eggs (I used two), for the bacon grease I substituted fat I rendered from leftover ham hocks, and I added 1/2 tsp of baking powder and 1/4 cup nutritional yeast. I flattened out the dough sprinkling liberally with more flour as I tri-folded three times (see Chef John's Buttermilk Biscuits recipe for example), then rolled the dough out to about 1/2 inch thick on a floured surface and sliced into bite-size pieces with a pizza wheel. Next time I'll try it with just one egg and maybe add some oats...

I used 3 c whole wheat flour, 1 c rolled oats and 1 c ground spent grain leftover from homebrewing. I used 3 eggs, threw in a small handful of shredded cheese and a little olive oil also. 
I rolled and cut it with small round cookie cutters about quarter sized for my pomeranians and about 2.5 inches in diameter for my labs. The poms are doing tricks wanting more after having one!

FUN! I made these as a project with my three year old niece, and she LOVED helping add the flour and the impromptu extra seasonings (like garlic powder and parsley.) She's even mastered the levers on my stand mixer which we used (dough hook) to mix it all up. The dough was not greasy like I thought it would be, and we hand-pressed it flat and used bone-shaped cookie cutters. They baked perfectly in 35 minutes, and somehow my dog knew these were for him when I took them out of the oven. I am thinking about selling these at a farmers' market this summer! Fun, fast, easy, kid-friendly baking recipe! Thanks!

Good basic biscuit recipe. Make as is or substitute white flour, rice flour, oats/oat flour, and/or potato flour for some of the white flour. I used a combination of 3 different kinds. You can use peanut butter as a substitute for all or part of the bacon fat, and applesauce for all or part of the milk. I used a spoon to flatten somewhat before baking, flipped them after bake time & baked them 3-4 minutes longer to make sure they were dry & crunchy. Our dog "Bruiser" loves them!

The dog loves them! I made a few revisions. Along with bacon, I added a jar of beef baby food, chicken broth for water, 1/2 tsp garlic powder and 1 cp peanut butter. My first batch baked at 350F for 35, they came out looking burnt. The second, I bake at 200F for 30 mins and then turned the oven off, leaving the cookies in the oven till cool. Tips: roll out small batches at a time as not to overwork the dough. I made 70 cookies.

This recipe was really easy to half, so I made one batch with bacon fat (no modifications) and one batch subbing peanut butter for the bacon fat. 

I used a small cookie cutter and baked for 35 minutes (pictured). The medium cookie cutter I baked for 38 minutes. They both turned out really well!

I've made these cookies several times now, as written and with several different variations. We're not bacon eaters, so I cooked up some turkey bacon, chopped up and added 1 c bacon bits, like you would chocolate chips. In the cases where I didn't use bacon grease (from local diner) I subbed 1/4 c vegetable oil. If I didn't use bacon, I have subbed 1c of cooked sweet potato(they LOVED it! who knew?) or 1c cheddar cheese (all but the pickiest liked this variation) 1c cooked leftover salmon. In all cases, I omitted the salt and added 1t baking powder. Will make again and again!

I used 2 T bacon drippings 4T olive/canola oil, as pork fat isn’t good for puggle. Also put in oats, peanut butter, and a handfull of shredded cheese. Rolled into balls, and made them look like mini peanut butter cooked. Dexter loves them.

My dog loves my bacon biscuits. I'm not sure how to rate this since I made more than a few changes: I crumbled & threw in the 16 oz bacon that rendered the fat. Other changes: used 3c ww flour + 1c quick cook oats + 1/2c flax seed + 1/2c wheat germ, used 3 eggs, used 1/2 c milk + 1 cup low sodium broth, eliminated salt.

I found it less tedious to flatten out dough to 1/4" and use a shot glass to cut out the biscuits. Baked 20 min on 2 cookie sheets, rotated 180 degrees and switched top and bottom cookie sheets and baked 10 minutes more. I made original recipe once and my recipe 3x. My recipe: if they're in my pocket, my dog will nose in and try to steal some!

These are great and my dogs love them. So, I just made two batches for an animal shelter bake sale! I rolled them out to 1/4 inch thick, cut them out with a tiny heart shaped cookie cutter, and baked them for about 18 minutes. It made a couple hundred and they turned out perfect. I did run out of whole wheat flour, so I substituted regular flour and wheat germ. It worked just fine.

I have babies(aka Dogs) who love these treats. They know when we cook bacon that means they are getting dog treats soon and don't leave until they get one. I added real bacon to it as well so they get that something extra. I put a paw print stamp on it
This is one of my princess favorite!

my pup LOVES these! i work for a restaurant that cooks bacon and tosses the grease, so i thought there must be SOMETHING to do with it otherwise. i made smaller balls (smaller pup) and found baking for 25 min was more than enough.

These were a bit for my daughter's furry girls! The finicky one was begging for more so she got a doggy bag for the trip home. Hanna may or may not share with sister Coco! Made as directed except for the flour. Used half all purpose and half light rye. Will be making again!
My dog will refuse to touch store bought treats when these are around. She stays next to me from the time I start making them until they are cooled and she gets the first one.
Dogs loved them. No change was made to the recipe.
I reduced the salt, as there’s more than enough salt in the bacon fat.
my dog definitely loved these....anything with bacon is a hit. I used white flour as I had no whole wheat.

These were so easy and both my dogs and my neighbors dogs loved them. Nice and crisp, don't fall apart. Only thing I changed was not adding salt as the bacon has enough salt. Might try broth next time instead of milk just to try. Otherwise these are the easiest and best dog cookies I've found. Trust me. Your dogs will live them.
